A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cognitive changes are moderately intercorrelated across domains and that this positive manifold is robust to a wide range of demographic, health, and genetic factors.
, even after controlling for a range of factors, aging-related change in one cognitive domain is related to aging-related change in other domains.
, even in the absence of a strong genetic component, aging-related changes are correlated across domains and that this correlation is not explained by demographic, health, or medical factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the fact that aging-related change is a complex phenomenon with many potential causes, there is a common factor underlying change across domains, and this common factor is not fully explained by the demographic, physical, medical, and genetic factors examined here.
the positive manifold of change is a robust phenomenon, but the underlying reasons for the positive manifold remain elusive.

, in contrast to previous research suggesting that cross-domain cognitive change is driven primarily by shared demographic and health factors, the present results suggest that cross-domain change is also driven by shared cognitive processes.
